sections.heading: D — Accuracy notes and source flags: pavement markings, signals and warning signs
sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: pavement markings, signals and warning signs
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical guide page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
These pages teach markings and signs mostly through pictures; the pictures were not described, and only written captions and text meanings were used (verify MO-MARK-D-SIGNIMAGES).
The shape and color key on the sign page is laid out as a picture legend; the pairings were read from its extracted caption text and restated [A04].
The left-turn lane and no passing zone illustrations carry no extractable detail beyond their captions [A01].
The School Crossing color transition is time-bound and isolated as dynamic [A05].
No sign image, symbol or arrow layout was invented or paraphrased from memory.

corpus_stability.reason: The Missouri Driver Guide prints a single edition line on its front cover (Revised August 2026); its table-of-contents note says law and policy changes may make parts out of date and points to the website for the current version, with no sign in the selected pages of more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical pages 44 to 50 show signs, signals and pavement markings as pictures with only short captions in the extracted text; any image-based recognition drill needs verified sign images from the guide's rendered pages or an official sign standard before it is built.
